issues.failure_explanation: For fixed finite M and n, there are only finitely many vectors a with |a|=n, so this family cannot span the infinite-dimensional space of all symmetric square-integrable kernels on \mathcal{T}_n. It is an orthonormal basis only of the finite-dimensional step-function subspace generated by the first M one-particle basis functions.

failure_location.quote: One can easily check that $(\widetilde{h}_{a})_{|a| = n}$ forms an orthonormal basis of $\widetilde{L}^{2}(\mathcal{T}_{n})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “an orthonormal basis of” by “an orthonormal basis of its finite-dimensional span” or “an orthonormal family in,” and describe convergence as M increases separately.
issues.overall_effect: The completeness assertion in the remark is false, although the later projection and approximation calculations only need orthonormality in the truncated subspace.
issues.title: A finite truncated tensor family is incorrectly claimed to be a basis of the full kernel space
issues.why_classification: This is a short local correction that does not alter the projection estimates or convergence rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $(Z_{s}^{\pi,\theta})_{s \in [t_{i-1}, t_{i})}$ is given by the martingale representation theorem applied to $\allowbreak\mathcal{C}^{\theta(i)}(F_{i}^{\pi, \theta})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme's martingale terminal value is \mathcal{C}^{\theta(i)}(F_i), which equals Y_{t_i}^{\pi,\theta}+\Delta_i\mathcal{C}^P(f_i), not Y_{t_i}^{\pi,\theta}+\Delta_i f_i. The proof therefore differentiates the wrong recursion. The displayed derivative estimates do not follow unless the projection is retained and its action on Malliavin derivatives is controlled.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the energy calculation for the correct term \mathcal{C}^P(f_i), using the derivative–projection identity and L2 contraction to recover a uniform bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the uniform Malliavin energy estimate and the ensuing uniform chaos-order truncation bound are incomplete, affecting both main error estimates.
issues.title: The Malliavin energy proof differentiates an equation not satisfied by the projected scheme
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial replacement argument is needed to propagate the derivative estimate through the projected recursion; merely editing the equation is insufficient.

Under Assumption \ref{assumption 1}, the random variable $\xi$ has absolute moments of fourth order, and hence $\mathbf{V}_{m}(\xi)$ can be proven to be finite.

issues.failure_explanation: Only Assumption 1 is adopted for the main estimates, but it gives merely \xi\in L^2 and a Lipschitz generator. The |\pi| Euler error invoked in the proof was stated only under the much stronger Assumption \ref{main assumption convergence rate}, including Malliavin and temporal regularity. Moreover, D\xi in the theorem need not exist. The subsequent assertion that Assumption 1 implies a fourth moment is false: L2 does not imply L4, so the Monte Carlo variance term \mathbf{V}_m(\xi) may also be infinite.
